title: Per-request inference metrics sidecar and label-scrubbing pipeline
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Background: We currently have multiple ad-hoc exporters producing per-request metrics for inference (latency, token counts, error codes) with inconsistent labels and high cardinality spikes for some tenants. This makes SLOs noisy and forces us to over‑aggregate, losing causal signal for root cause analysis. Goal: Introduce a lightweight per-request sidecar that normalizes OTel spans/metrics, applies deterministic label-scrubbing and cardinality rules, and exports both Prometheus-friendly metric envelopes and OTLP envelopes for long-term storage. The pipeline must preserve enough context for causal latency attribution while bounding label cardinality to avoid prometheus series explosion.

Scope and non-goals:
- In scope: a sidecar deployed alongside inference runtime containers (hosted + dedicated nodes), a canonical label map and scrub policy, deterministic sampling of high-cardinality attributes, a Prometheus scrape-adapter for short-lived envelopes, OTLP forwarding to long-term store, and dashboards for per-route SLOs.
- Out of scope: full-blown tenant-specific aggregation rules (handled later in a separate project), SDK-level instrumentation changes (we will add shims but not change app code in this ticket).

Design decisions / key requirements:
1) Sidecar responsibilities:
   - Observe each request lifecycle via tracing hooks and local span reader.
   - Produce 1 small, high-cardinality-aware envelope per request that includes route, model_family, model_version, duration_ms, tokens_in, tokens_out, status_code, failure_reason (scrubbed), cache_hit boolean, and sampling_decision.
   - Emit two outputs: (A) a Prometheus-compatible metrics envelope (push via a lightweight gateway or expose scrape endpoint on sidecar) with stable metric names and normalized labels; (B) OTLP span + metric export to the telemetry backend for deep analysis.
2) Label canonicalization and scrub policy:
   - Maintain a canonical label map documented in this ticket (route => route_id, model => family/version, tenant_id hashed to tenant_bucket for SLO bucketing, request_id retained for trace linking only).
   - Strip PII and free-form input text from metrics. Replace any discovered long or unrecognized labels with reserved value "_redacted".
   - Use deterministic bucketing for high-cardinality labels (e.g., prompt hash 16 buckets) to allow heatmap analysis without unbounded growth.
3) Sampling & cardinality control:
   - Deterministic sampling: 1/1000 full payload exports for attestation + 100% of errors and tail-latency requests (p99.9) for full context.
   - Support config-driven sampling rate per deployment tier (hosted vs dedicated) via configmaps in k8s.
4) Backpressure & resilience:
   - Sidecar will buffer up to 10k envelopes in-memory with an LRU eviction that increments an internal "sidecar_evicted" metric. On exporter failure, switch to a bounded disk-backed spool (max 100MB) and expose healthcheck indicating degraded export.
5) Prometheus shaping:
   - Expose a compact scrape endpoint with pre-aggregated counters/gauges to avoid high cardinality timeseries. Provide an optional push gateway for edge nodes where scrape is infeasible.
6) Compatibility and incremental rollout:
   - Must be compatible with existing Prometheus rules and dashboards; provide a translation layer to present old metric names as aliases for 90 days.
   - Rollout via canary on 5% of nodes in staging, then 20% production, monitor sidecar_evicted and series_count per-pod.

Acceptance criteria:
- Sidecar image built and deployed to staging with config driven by k8s configmap.
- Canonical label map documented and checked in (docs link below).
- Unit tests for label-scrub rules and deterministic bucketing with >95% coverage of rule branches.
- E2E test that generates 10k requests and validates series count remains under configured threshold and that 100% of errors are exported in full.
- Prometheus scrape endpoint returns stable metric names and no more than X series per pod (X defined in config).
- Dashboards: per-route latency and error rate panels updated to consume the new envelopes without gaps; alerting on sidecar_evicted > 10/min.

Telemetry and dashboards to update:
- latency/per_route_p95, p99 panels should switch to new metric (route_latency_ms_bucket) with alias mapping from old metrics.
- error-rate per route: route_errors_total with labels {route_id, error_class}
- operational panels: sidecar_evicted, sidecar_export_queue_depth, sidecar_disk_spool_usage

Implementation notes and artifacts:
- Sidecar prototype in repo: git@github.com:redwood-inference/telemetry-sidecars.git (branch: eng/ENG-556677-sidecar)
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/TELEMETRY/Per-Request+Sidecar+Design
- Draft PR for sidecar server and Prometheus adapter: https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry-sidecars/pull/84
- Test harness for synthetic load: scripts/loadtest/per_request_emitter.py

Migration and rollback plan:
- Canary rollout: deploy to 5% nodes with verbose logs, run synthetic litmus (see tests). If sidecar_evicted > 5/min or series_count grows > threshold, pause rollout and roll back.
- If OTLP export backend rejects envelopes, sidecar flips to no-op metrics and sets degraded_health and we trigger automated fallback to legacy exporter.

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- Where to compute tenant_bucket: sidecar vs prior layer? Sidecar chosen to avoid changes to runtime but increases cross-tenant variance in bucket mapping; we need to validate hashing seed across nodes.
- Disk spool size vs memory: we chose small disk spool to avoid OOM risk for edge nodes; ops asked whether 100MB is sufficient for bursty workloads.
- Cost of deterministic sampling for tail traces: storage impact must be measured; we plan a 14-day retention for full payloads.

Next steps:
- Finalize canonical label map and scrub regexes (action: Diego, due 2026-03-05).
- Land unit tests and PR for sidecar basic pipeline (action: Diego/Aisha, target 2026-03-12).
- Create dashboard migration PR and run synthetic load in staging (action: Observability team, target 2026-03-18).
